name: Scout
body:
The scout is a mobile skirmisher and stealthy master of reconnaissance. They focus on moving fast, moving quietly, and striking when the enemy least expects it.

They are a combatant that uses mobility to survive rather than standing and fighting against targets.

Class Details

Role: The scout is a skilled character intended to maximize hit and run tactics. As a class caught between the rogue and ranger, the scout can be a formidable ambusher and wilderness guide but can also be easily at home in urban environments. The scout is excellent at pinning down single targets, dealing good damage and escaping unscathed. With excellent skills, mobility, and stealth as well as reliable ways to deal additional damage, the scout is sure to aid any party.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 4d6 x 10 (140 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The scout’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Disable Device (Dex), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 8 + Int modifier

Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Features

2nd	+1	+3	+3	+0	Adrenaline rush +1

5th	+3	+4	+4	+1	Blindsense 10 ft.
6th	+4	+5	+5	+2	Bonus combat feat, unhindered steps

8th	+6/+1	+6	+6	+2	Adrenaline rush +2, covert expert, improved uncanny dodge
9th	+6/+1	+6	+6	+3	Improved hit and run
10th	+7/+2	+7	+7	+3	Astounding grit, blindsense 30 ft., sneak attack +4d6
11th	+8/+3	+7	+7	+3	Deeds, fast movement +20
12th	+9/+4	+8	+8	+4	Bonus combat feat

Class Features

The following are the class features of the scout.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A scout is proficient with all simple weapons, plus the handaxe, throwing axe, battleaxe, light hammer, longbow, and shortbow, including the composite version of both bows. They are proficient with light armor, and shields (except tower shields).

Trapfinding (Ex)

At 1st level a scout gains a bonus on Perception checks to locate traps and on Disable Device checks equal to 1/2 their class level. A scout may use Disable Device to disarm magic traps.

Sneak Attack (Ex)

At 1st level, if a scout can catch an opponent when they are unable to defend themselves effectively from the attack, the scout can strike a vital spot for extra damage.

The scout’s attack deals extra damage anytime their target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not), or when the scout flanks their target. This extra damage is 1d6 at 1st level, and increases by 1d6 at 3rd level every three scout levels thereafter. Should the scout score a critical hit with a sneak attack, this extra damage is not multiplied. Ranged attacks can count as sneak attacks only if the target is within 30 feet.

With a weapon that deals non-lethal damage (like a sap, whip, or an unarmed strike), a scout can make a sneak attack that deals non-lethal damage instead of lethal damage. They cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal non-lethal damage in a sneak attack, not even with the usual –4 penalty.

The scout must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot. A scout cannot sneak attack while striking a creature with concealment.

Grit (Ex)

At 1st level, a scout makes their mark upon the world with daring deeds. Some scouts claim they belong to the most difficult method of combat, but it’s more likely that the volatile nature of their craft simply prunes the unlucky and careless, leaving only the most cunning. Whatever the reason, all scouts have grit. In game terms, grit is a fluctuating measure of a scout’s ability to perform amazing actions in combat. A scout begins each day with an amount or grit equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). The amount of grit a scout has may go up and down throughout the day but they can never have more grit then their Wisdom modifier. A scout can regain 1 grit point in the following ways, and only one per per round.

Whenever the scout scores a critical hit after moving at least 10 feet in a round.
Whenever the scout reduces an enemy to 0 or fewer hit points after moving at least 10 feet in a round.
Whenever they double move during combat with no other actions.
Deeds (Ex)

Scouts spend grit points to accomplish deeds. Most deeds grant the scout a momentary bonus or effect, but some provide longer-lasting effects. Some deeds remain in effect while the scout has at least 1 grit point, but do not require expending grit to be maintained. A scout can only perform deeds of their level or lower. Unless otherwise noted, a deed can be performed multiple successive times, as long as the scout has or spends the required number of grit points to perform the deed.

The following deeds are available to the scout at 1st level.

Covert Finesse (Ex)

A scout can spend 1 grit point when they make an Acrobatics, Climb, Escape Artist, or Stealth check to roll 1d6 and add the result to the check. They can do this after they make the check but before the result is revealed. If the result of the d6 roll is a natural 6, they roll another 1d6 and add it to the check. They can continue to do this as long as they roll natural 6s, up to a number of times equal to their Dexterity modifier (minimum 1).

Lucky Break (Ex)

A scout can spend 1 grit point as an immediate action to add a bonus to their AC and CMD equal to their Wisdom modifier until their next turn.

Scout’s Determination (Ex)

A scout with at least 1 grit point gains a +2 bonus on saves or checks made against ongoing conditions, such as bleed, mind control, or possession.

Skirmisher (Ex)

As long as the scout has at least 1 grit point they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC, Reflex saves and CMD as long as they moved at least 10 ft on their turn. This bonus lasts until the start of their next turn and increases by an additional +1 at 4th level and every 4 class levels thereafter to a maximum of +6 at 20th level. The scout may spend 1 grit point as a swift action after moving 10 ft on their turn; if they do, any attacks made before the beginning of their next turn are treated as satisfying the conditions for sneak attack.

The following deeds are available to the scout at 3rd level.

Kip-Up (Ex)

At 3rd level, while the scout has at least 1 grit point, they can kip-up from prone as a move action without provoking an attack of opportunity. They can kip-up as a swift action instead by spending 1 grit point.

Scout’s Initiative (Ex)

While the scout has at least 1 grit point, they gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks. In addition, if they have the Quick Draw feat, their hands are free and unrestrained, and they have any single light or one-handed weapon, a bow, or crossbow that isn’t hidden, they can draw that weapon as part of the initiative check.

Scout’s Evasion (Ex)

While the scout has at least 1 grit point whenever they succeed on a Reflex saving throw against an attack which would have a reduced effect on a successful save, instead they suffer no effect. When rolling a Reflex saving throw the scout may spend 1 grit point as an immediate action. If they do, until the beginning of their next turn whenever they fail a Reflex saving throw against an attack, spell, or effect that would have a reduced effect on a successful save, they suffer the reduced effect instead of the full effect.

Trick Shot (Ex)

While the scout has at least 1 grit point, whenever they attack with a thrown weapon, that weapon is treated as having a non-magical version of the returning weapon property as long as the attack was made against a target within 30 ft. The scout may also spend 1 grit point as a swift action when making an attack roll with a thrown or ranged weapon to cause it to bounce or ricochet, and make two attacks with that weapon; these attacks may be against the same target or against any two targets within 15 feet of each other and both within 30 feet of the scout.

The following deeds are available to scouts at 7th level.

Canny Resilience (Ex)

While the scout has at least 1 grit point available they are treated as having the Diehard feat. While below 0 hit points if the scout successfully deals damage to an opponent with a weapon attack they may expend 1 grit point to restore a number of hit points to bring their hit point total to 1.

Leaf on the Wind (Ex)

The scout may spend 1 grit as a move action to be treated as though under the effects of a non-magical haste effect for a number of rounds equal to their Wisdom modifier.

Sudden Strike (Ex)

The scout takes extra advantage of unaware opponents. As long as the scout has at least 1 grit point they gain a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls against opponents who are denied their Dexterity bonus to AC. When attacking an opponent denied their Dexterity bonus to AC the scout may spend 1 grit point as a swift action to gain a competence bonus on attack and damage rolls against that target equal to 1/4 their class level until the beginning to their next turn.

Vital Momentum (Ex)

While the scout has at least 1 grit point they are considered to possess the Vital Strike feat. The scout may spend 1 grit point to apply Vital Strike to one attack made in conjunction with Spring Attack or Shot on the Run. At 15th level, as long as the scout has at least 1 grit point they are treated as having Improved Vital Strike and may spend 1 grit point as a free action to apply Improved Vital Strike to one attack made in conjunction with Spring Attack or Shot on the Run.

The following deeds are available to scouts at 11th level.

Combat Acumen (Ex)

As a move action, the scout may spend 1 grit and make a Sense Motive check against a creature they can see. The DC for this check is 10 + the creature’s Wisdom bonus + its base attack bonus. If this check succeeds the scout learns what combat feats the creature has access to. By spending an additional 1 grit point when making this check the scout can choose a single combat feat possessed by the target to be unaffected by for 1 minute. For example if a creature has Power Attack and the scout were to choose it with this deed, that creature would be unable to benefit from the Power Attack damage against the scout for 1 minute, but they still take the penalty to attack if used.

Startling Strike (Ex)

The scout can spend 2 grit points when making an attack against any target within 30 feet. When they do, they compare the attack roll to the target’s CMD, if the attack roll is higher the scout may apply one of the following conditions to the target of their attack.

The target is staggered for one round.
The target is knocked prone. This can knock a flying creature to the ground if they are less than 60 feet in the air. This otherwise has no effect on creatures which cannot be tripped.
The target halves all movement speeds it possesses for a number of rounds equal to the scout’s Wisdom modifier.
The target drops one held or carried item of the scout’s choice unless it is firmly secured to the creature such as with a locked gauntlet.
Subtle Steps (Ex)

The scout may spend 1 grit point when making a 5 foot step to instead make a 10 foot step.

The following deeds are available to scouts of 15th level.

Focused Ambush (Ex)

Whenever the scout uses Improved Spring Attack, Greater Spring Attack, Improved Shot on the Run, or Greater Shot on the Run, they may spend 1 grit point as a free action to target a single creature with each attack rather than separate creatures.

Rending Wound (Ex)

Once per round when the scout deals damage with a weapon attack, they may spend 1 grit point as a free action to add an amount of bleed damage to that attack equal to their Dexterity modifier.

Alternatively the scout can spend 2 grit points to deal 1 bleed damage to either the creature’s Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution scores.

Unbound (Ex)

The scout may spend 2 grit points as a standard action to gain the benefits of freedom of movement for a number of minutes equal to their Wisdom modifier.

The following deeds are available to scouts of 19th level.

Deadly Vanguard (Ex)

As long as the scout has at least 2 grit points they increase the critical threat range of any weapon they wield with which they are proficient by 1. This increase stacks with effects such as Improved Critical but is applied after all other effects have been applied. Whenever the scout confirms a critical hit they may spend 2 grit points and apply one of the following effects, each effect allows for a saving throw with a DC of 20 + the scout’s Dexterity modifier.

The target is paralyzed for 2d4 rounds unless they succeed at a Fortitude save.
The target is knocked prone and staggered for 2d6 rounds unless they succeed at a Reflex save.
The target is knocked unconscious for 2d4 minutes unless they succeed at a Fortitude save.
The target is confused for 2d4 rounds unless they succeed at a Will save.
Rapid Strikes (Ex)

Whenever the scout uses the full attack action, they may spend 2 grit points as a swift action to gain two additional attacks at their highest base attack bonus. These bonus attacks can be made in addition to those granted by haste and similar abilities. Alternatively, the scout may spend 2 grit points as a full round action to make an attack against each enemy creature within their threatened area or within 30 ft if using a thrown or ranged weapon. These attacks are made at the scout’s highest base attack bonus.

Tenacious Grit (Ex)

As long as the scout has at least 1 grit point they can avoid an attack that would slay them outright. When targeted by any effect which would result in death or similar permanent consequences and allows a saving throw, such as petrification, the scout rolls twice and takes the better result.

Adrenaline Rush (Ex)

At 2nd level, the scout can be prepared for combat at a moment’s notice. Whenever initiative is rolled, if the scout has 2 or fewer grit points they gain 1 temporary grit point that is spent first when using deeds that rely on grit. These temporary grit points disappear when initiative ends. At 8th level and again at 14th level and 20th level the number of temporary grit granted by this ability increases by 1.

Fast Movement (Ex)

At 3rd level, the scout gains a +10 foot bonus to their movement speed. At 11th level and again at 19th level this bonus to movement speed increases by an additional +10 feet.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 4th level, a scout can react to danger before their senses would normally allow. They cannot be caught flat-footed, nor do they lose their Dex bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. The scout still loses their Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A scout with this ability can still lose their Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action. If the scout already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Trackless Step (Ex)

Starting at 4th level, a scout leaves no trail in natural surroundings and cannot be tracked. They may choose to leave a trail if so desired.

Hit and Run (Ex)

At 4th level, the scout gains Spring Attack and Shot on the Run as bonus feats without meeting their prerequisites.

Blindsense (Ex)

At 5th level, the scout gains blindsense as the universal monster ability with a range of 10ft. At 10th level, this becomes blindsense 30 ft.

Unhindered Steps (Ex)

Starting at 6th level, a scout can move through any sort of terrain that slows movement, such as undergrowth, rubble, and similar terrain, at their normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. This ability does not let the scout move more quickly through terrain that requires a Climb or Swim check to navigate, nor can they move more quickly through terrain or undergrowth that has been magically manipulated to impede motion.

Combat Feat (Ex)

At 6th, 12th and 18th levels the scout gains a bonus combat feat.

Covert Expert (Ex)

At 8th level, the scout is a master of blending in. The scout can move at full speed while using Stealth without penalty.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

A scout of 8th level or higher can no longer be flanked.

This defense denies another creature the ability to sneak attack the scout by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least four more levels than the target does in a class that grants sneak attack.

If a character already has uncanny dodge, see above, from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum level required to flank the character.

Improved Hit and Run (Ex)

At 9th level, the scout gains Improved Spring Attack and Improved Shot on the Run* as bonus feats without needing to meet its prerequisites.

Astounding Grit (Ex)

At 10th level the scout has survived countless lucky scrapes and close calls, their grit pool increases to hold twice their Wisdom modifier and they begin each day with this amount of grit.

Greater Hit and Run (Ex)

At 15th level, the scout gains Greater Spring Attack and Greater Shot on the Run* as a bonus feat without meeting its prerequisites.

Hide in Plain Sight (Ex)

At 17th level, the scout can move unseen by even the most attentive eyes. They can make Stealth checks even while being observed.

Blindsight (Ex)

At 20th level, the scout gains blindsight as the universal monster ability of the same name with a range of 30 ft.
